Subject: Implementation & timeline questions for Redwood integration

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Helios is excited about Redwood's latency and routing guarantees. Procurement asked I follow up with a few hard requirements that will determine whether we can include Redwood in our Q3 rollout. High level: we need deterministic routing to a residency lane, per-request audit export hooks (S3/HTTPS), and confirmation of dedicated capacity during the pilot window.

Specifically:
- Deterministic routing: our compliance team requires that requests from our prod tenant are always routed to a pinned residency pool in us-east-1. Does Redwood have a supported path for that now, and what are the tradeoffs?
- Audit exports: we need an export that contains per-request metadata (trace id, model, token counts, user id, timestamp) delivered to our S3 bucket or an HTTPS endpoint, with encryption in transit.
- Dedicated capacity: we are prepared to sign for reserved capacity during pilot but need timelines for warm pool readiness.

Attached is a draft SOW and a short list of compliance items (Helios_SOW_v1.pdf). Our procurement window closes 06/15 — if we can get a firm yes on feasibility and an outline of a delivery plan by 05/26, we can move forward quickly.

Can you loop in the engineering/product folks and advise? Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

Thanks,
Danielle Wu
Head of Integrations, Helios Financial

Thanks — did a quick tech review after the demo and the asks map to two different effort tracks. High-level summary:

Option A — Minimal-shim (recommended as phased approach)
- Implement a routing configuration shim that maps Helios tenant IDs to a residency lane at the routing layer. This requires config + routing policy enforcement but avoids touching model kernels.
- ETA: ~6 weeks (4w dev + 1w test + 1w rollout + warm pool lead time).
- Audit export: can be implemented in parallel as a 2-week effort (export hook + schema + S3/HTTPS delivery).
- Tradeoffs: lower risk; does not guarantee absolute determinism under extreme autoscale events — needs clear SLAs for capacity pull-through.

Option B — Dedicated routing lane (more invasive)
- Changes to runtime to enforce hard-affinity residency for tenant requests, with eviction/rebalance semantics.
- ETA: ~12 weeks (includes infra changes and end-to-end validation).
- Tradeoffs: stronger guarantee but longer delivery and higher ops cost.

Recommendation: propose a phased mutual action plan — ship audit export and config-based routing shim first (ships within 6 weeks), validate pilot, then evaluate Dedicated lane as an optional second phase. We'll need Product/Engineering priority for the shim and two full-time engineers for 4 weeks.

Open questions:
- Do we have budget sign-off to allocate 2 FTEs for the initial 4-week sprint?
- Any Helios-specific encryption or retention constraints beyond the SOW?

I'll draft a short tech note to include in the reply to Helios.

—Karthik
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Adding engineering detail for the proposed phased approach.

We can prototype the routing shim and the audit export concurrently. Rough engineering asks:
- Routing shim prototype: 3 engineers (2 backend, 1 infra) for 3 weeks to produce a canary-capable shim that supports tenant->residency mapping and basic affinity heuristics. Deliverables: routing-config API, integration tests, canary runbook.
- Audit export: 1 engineer for 2 weeks to expose per-request hooks (trace_id, model, tokens, tenant_id, timestamp), wire to S3/HTTPS with retry/backoff and HMAC-signed delivery option. Deliverables: schema (attached audit-export-schema.json), sample consumer config and runbook.
- Warm pool: Ops will need a minimum of 10 days lead time after capacity request to provision and run a warm pool for the pilot. Cost estimate depends on reservation length; ops/finance to provide number.

We can have a technical prototype demo ready in ~3 weeks (week of 06/12) if leadership prioritizes the work and approves temporary FTE allocation. I'll attach a simple architecture diagram for the shim (routing-proposal-diagram.png).

If Sales can confirm the DocuSign timeline and any binding budget commitment, we can lock the sprint and meet Helios' procurement window.

Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
